# Results — Study 271 (Cardboard-Box) on ^GSPC annual price returns

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Box/rail-freight growth is
hardcoded in [`data.py`](../cardboard_box/data.py) (1970–2024, 55 years). S&P 500
returns are December/December **price** returns of ^GSPC from Yahoo, cached at
`_cache/gspc_annual.parquet` (price-only, dividends excluded). The predictor for year Y
is matched to the S&P return for year **Y+1** (one-year forecast lag — no look-ahead).
Match the fingerprint below to confirm you hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC (Yahoo, nominal price, Dec/Dec) | returns 1971–2025 | 55 years | `15cf4dbe0618` |
| Box / rail-freight growth table | output 1970–2024 | 55 years | hardcoded constant |

The fingerprint hashes the `fwd_return` column of the forecast frame (box predictor).

## Forecast regression — does this year's freight forecast next year's market?

Model: `gspc_return[Y+1] = alpha + beta * freight_growth[Y] + eps`, slope t-stat under
a Newey-West (Bartlett, 1 lag) HAC covariance.

| Predictor | slope beta | HAC t | R² | Pearson r (p) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Box shipments** | **-0.0109** | **-1.605** | 4.5% | -0.212 (0.120) |
| **Rail carloads** | -0.0074 | -1.805 | 4.3% | — |

- Both slopes are **negative** — the *opposite* of the bullish "boxes-up → market-up"
  story — and both |t| < 2. There is no forecasting signal, and what little slope exists
  leans the wrong way (a faint mean-reversion, not momentum).
- Conditional next-year means: after a year of **positive** box growth, the S&P returned
  **+9.84%** on average; after **negative** box growth, **+8.59%** — a 1.25pp gap, well
  inside sampling noise (n = 42 vs 13).

## Coincident control — same-year freight vs same-year market

| Regression | HAC t | R² | Pearson r |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Box growth[Y] → S&P return[Y] | **-0.068** | 0.000 | -0.007 |

Even the *contemporaneous* link is essentially zero. The series share the broad
recession dips, but the year-to-year wiggles of box growth and annual equity returns
barely correlate — so there isn't even a coincident correlation to mistake for a lead.

## Timing strategy — long next year iff box growth > 0 (10 bps one-way cost on NAV)

| Strategy | Annualised (price-only) | Turnover | Invested |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy & hold | **+8.15%/yr** | — | 100% |
| Box timer, gross | +6.57%/yr | 0.31 flips/yr | 76.4% |
| Box timer, net (10 bps) | **+6.54%/yr** | 0.31 flips/yr | 76.4% |

- **Net minus buy-and-hold: −1.61pp/yr.** The timer loses.
- Timer hit-rate **61.8%** is *below* the unconditional up-rate **74.6%** — keying on
  box growth is worse than always being long. Costs are tiny (low turnover); the
  shortfall is the opportunity cost of sitting in cash after weak box prints that are
  *not* reliably followed by down markets.

## Power check

With n = 55 and one regressor, the minimum detectable forecasting correlation at 80%
power (two-sided, α = 0.05) is **|r| ≈ 0.37**. The observed box-forecast |r| is **0.21**
— below the threshold *and* wrong-signed. n = 55 annual observations cannot resolve a
weak forecasting relationship, and there is no strong one to resolve.

## Positive control (synthetic)

On a synthetic (freight, next-year-return) panel with a planted forecasting `beta`, the
HAC regression recovers the slope and the t-stat clears 2 once the beta is real and n is
adequate. The engine is honest; the real tape (t = −1.6) simply has no signal.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Forecast slope box HAC t = −1.61 (wrong sign), rail t = −1.81,
  coincident t = −0.07; no |t| ≥ 2 anywhere; R² of the forecast regression 4.5%.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The box timer earns 6.5%/yr net vs 8.2%/yr buy-and-hold and
  has a hit-rate below the unconditional up-rate. No tradable edge over passive exposure.
- **Busted — a coincident gauge dressed as a leading one.** Box and rail output genuinely
  track the economy (they dip in every recession), but the stock market has already priced
  the expected economy; a slow annual macro series carries no forecasting content for it.
